subject: [Bugfix] Fix support for dimension like integers and ScalarType (#9299)
pr_body:
Some of the custom ops take integers which are `Tensor` dimensions.  These can sometimes be `SymInt`s if those `Tensor` dimensions are marked as dynamic.  The appropriate `int` arguments for these class of custom ops have been changed to `SymInt` to support dynamic dimensions.

The inductor is not currently able to support passing custom C++ classes to custom ops.  This PR fully implements `ScalarType` in python.  `ScalarType`s are now passed by `id` to C++ where they are reconstructed into C++ `ScalarType`s.  This has the side effect of removing the `_core_C` extension.

fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/9234

cc @SageMoore , @ProExpertProg , @LucasWilkinson , @youkaichao

subject: [ROCm][AITER] Hotfix for `memory access fault` errors in AITER triton MOE routing (#50859)
pr_body:
Companion AITER fix: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4530 (making this PR fix redundant once the AITER fix is merged, released, and AITER pin in vLLM is updated).

## Purpose

This PR hot-fixes

```
tests/models/quantization/test_gpt_oss.py::test_gpt_oss_attention_quantization[amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8-0.89-1]
```

that started failing in ROCm vLLM following AITER version bump from `0.1.16.post5` to `0.1.19` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49361) as seen in [mi355_1: Quantized Models Test](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11528/list?sid=019fb767-0fce-4570-b9af-a4ba0421b3d5&tab=output), with:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x3a0749c0) on address 0x7de557bcb000. Reason: Unknown.
^[_bk;t=1785489648144 GPU coredump: execvp failed: No such file or directory
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 Failed to write program header to pipe: Broken pipe
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 GPU coredump: handler exited with error (status: 1)
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 GPU core dump failed
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

Previously passing, e.g. see https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11474/list.

Also confirmed locally that vLLM main + AITER `0.1.16.post5` does not cause the issue.

## Context

To make it short: a seemingly harmless change in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4198 resulted in AITER's triton MOE routing to start to wrongfully handle token rows containing `inf`/`-inf`/`nan`, which is the case with HIP Graph in vLLM (e.g. `tokens_unpadded=7`, `tokens_padded=8` to dispatch on a recorded graph, and the last row containing dummy meaningless data).

Graph replays in vLLM when using padding thus started resulting in `memory access fault`.

See more context in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4530

## Test Plan

```bash

pytest tests/models/quantization/test_gpt_oss.py::test_aiter_mxfp4_moe_ignores_padded_rows
```

## Test Result

Both tests result in `memory access fault` on `main`, and pass with this fix.

subject: [BugFix][Router Replay] Capture Logical Experts with EPLB (#33013)
pr_body: ## Purpose In the latest vLLM code, the routed experts capture logic is broken, asRoutedExpertsCapturer.create() runs after model construction (during KV-cache init), but FusedMoE only binds self.capture in init. subject: [Bugfix][Flashinfer] fix VLLM_USE_TRTLLM_ATTENTION issue for models with diff hyperparameters (#25924)
pr_body:
## Purpose

- Issue: for the models with diff hyperparameters(`window_left`, `logits_soft_cap`, `sm_scale`) to use flashinfer backend, we always need to set `VLLM_USE_TRTLLM_ATTENTION=1` to bypass hyperparameters check in `infer_global_hyperparameters()`
  - `VLLM_USE_TRTLLM_ATTENTION` should not be used directly to determine TRTLLM attention is used or not. Should use `prefill_use_trtllm` and `decode_use_trtllm` instead.
- This PR delayed the checking in `infer_global_hyperparameters()`, moving it after trtllm attn usage is determined.
- Replace all `supports_trtllm_attention` usage with `can_use_trtllm_attention`

## Test Plan && Test Result
On main, running gpt-oss eagle3 without `VLLM_USE_TRTLLM_ATTENTION=1` will encounter:
```
AssertionError: FlashInfer backend currently only supports models in which alllayers share the same values for the following hyperparameters:`window_left`, `logits_soft_cap`, `sm_scale`.
```
After the PR, no need to set `VLLM_USE_TRTLLM_ATTENTION=1`.

---

subject: Fix eplb nvfp4 experts hook (#37217)

## Summary

Two fixes for EPLB + NVFP4 quantization on FlashInfer modular kernels (CuteDSL/CUTLASS/TRTLLM):

subject: [AMD] fix: use the hardware fp8 e4m3 convert on gfx950 (#37140)
pr_body:
## Motivation


`pack_fp8` is the fp8 quantization step in the DSv4, DSv3.2-indexer, MiniMax and Kimi-K3 kernels. On ROCm it is a hand-written bit twiddle, and it converts part of its input range wrong.

The overflow check is `exp8 >= kMaxExp`, and that is off by one. `exp8 == kMaxExp` is not overflow, it is the top exponent of the format, and e4m3 holds plenty of values there. So on gfx950 everything from 256 to 448 gets written out as 448. At the bottom of that range, that is 75% too big. Rounding is biased upward as well: ties go away from zero instead of to even, and one bf16 input in sixteen lands exactly on a tie.

This is not an edge case. Every caller picks a scale that puts its largest element at or just under the format maximum, which is exactly where the broken range sits. With a ue8m0 scale, about 4.5% of a group of 64 falls in it. With the plain fp32 amax scale that the indexer paths use, the maximum lands on 448 every single time, and the figure is 11.4%.

Nobody caught this because a wrong byte does not look like a bug from outside. Every caller quantizes `value * inv_scale`, so a bad conversion just makes fp8 look lossier than expected. No NaN, no crash, no failing test. And the conversion had never been tested on its own, only inside fused kernels that cannot tell a bad byte from ordinary quantization loss.

While gfx950 and gfx12xx can do this in hardware. `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32` converts two floats to e4m3 with round-to-nearest-even in a single instruction, HIP exposes it as `__hip_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2`, and this tree already uses the scalar form in `per_token_quant_fp8.cu`. This PR just routes those archs through it.


## Modifications


There are two copies of this cast in the tree. Each gets a new branch, and neither existing implementation is touched.

* `jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/fp8_utils.cuh` (+23 / −2). The software cast becomes the `#else`. The two deleted lines are a stale comment above it.

* `aot/csrc/elementwise/dsv4_norm_rope.cu` (+12 / −0). The same branch, added as an `#elif` between the CUDA one and this file's own copy of the cast.

  Why this file needs its own branch rather than including the share …[truncated]

subject: [Fix] Correct W4AFP8 DeepEP scaling and mode-specific dtypes (#33669)
pr_body:
## Motivation

W4AFP8 with DeepEP had two independent failures in the same normal/prefill path.

First, `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal` called `deepep_post_reorder_triton_kernel` without the required `routed_scaling_factor`, causing the original first-request `TypeError` in #33660. The model forward applies routed scaling after the cross-rank DeepEP combine, so this rank-local reduction must receive the neutral value `1.0`; using the model factor here would scale twice.

After the first fix, the reporter reproduced a second failure on 4xH200: DeepEP `intranode.cu:926` reported `Unsupported type`. That line is the normal **combine** dtype switch, not an INT4-weight dispatch site; DeepEP only transports activations and its normal combine accepts BF16. The actual problem was SGLang's dtype selection:

- W4AFP8 normal/prefill requantizes BF16 activations with checkpoint static scales, so its DeepEP payload must remain BF16.
- W4AFP8 low-latency/decode consumes DeepEP FP8 activations together with per-token-group scales, so that payload must remain FP8.
- With `--deepep-mode auto`, the previous global default selected FP8 for both implementations. The normal W4AFP8 path discarded the returned FP8 scale; a zero-token expert rank then returned an FP8 tensor directly to DeepEP's BF16-only normal combine, producing the reported assertion. Globally forcing BF16 would fix prefill but break low-latency decode.

subject: [Bugfix] ep_scatter kernel store-load race condition (#34991)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an intra-CTA data race in `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_1` that causes sporadic "Warp Illegal Address" crashes during DeepGEMM MoE permutation (observed on DeepSeek V3 PD decode, but possibly affects any EP path using this kernel).

### The bug

The kernel launches 256 blocks × 256 threads (8 warps). Each block computes an exclusive prefix sum and writes **all** 256 entries of `expert_start_loc` to global memory via a vector `tl.store`, then loads back one entry via `tl.load(expert_start_loc + cur_expert)`.

The kernel distributes the vector store across threads, so thread `k` writes element `k`. With 8 warps, the store and load are not separated with a memory barrier. When block N loads `expert_start_loc[N]`, thread 0 (warp 0) may execute the load before thread N (warp N/32) commits its store. Since `expert_start_loc` is allocated with `torch.empty()` (uninitialized), the stale read returns garbage, which is used as an offset into `m_indices`. This causes a crash with an illegal address.

### The fix

Extract `cur_expert_start` from the prefix-sum register vector via `tl.sum(tl.where(...))` (a warp-shuffle reduction), then store that scalar to `expert_start_loc[cur_expert]`. This replaces the old pattern of writing a full 256-element vector to global memory and loading one element back. The scalar is used directly from registers (no race), and each block writes only its own entry to `expert_start_loc` (no redundancy). The next kernel sees the correct values via the implicit kernel-launch barrier.

### No need for pipelining

This PR also removes software pipeline staging in the later loop, because the loop only performs simple store and does not benefit from pipelining.

## Test Plan

This issue is not very easy to reproduce though, and I only observe it very occasionally. However, one can build a minimal reproduce example following the same pattern (vector `tl.store` + scalar `tl.load` on an uninitialized buffer) and see the data race after repeating several times.

Unit tests: `pytest -s tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` -- all passed.

subject: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix batch invariance in RMSNorm kernels by pinning block size (#48391)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a batch-invariance gap in the `fused_add_rms_norm` CUDA kernel.

The kernel selects its block size from the token count: `max_block_size = (num_tokens < 256) ? 1024 : 256`, independent of whether batch-invariant mode is enabled. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the residual RMSNorm path (`RMSNorm.forward_cuda` with a residual → `ops.fused_add_rms_norm`) routes to this kernel. As a result the *same* token reduces with `block=1024` when processed in a small batch (`num_tokens < 256`) but with `block=256` inside a batch of `>= 256` tokens. The two block sizes give different `cub::BlockReduce` partitions and therefore a different fp32 sum-of-squares order, so the normalized output is not bit-exact across batch sizes whenever
`hidden_size > 256`.

The existing `batch_invariant_launch` flag only disabled vectorization (width 8 → 0); it did not touch the block size. This PR locks `max_block_size` to 1024 when `vllm_is_batch_invariant()` is true, making the reduction width independent of `num_tokens`.

This is a follow-up to #40413 (which routed the residual path to `fused_add_rms_norm` on the assumption it is already batch-invariant) and is tracked under #27433. It is not a duplicate: no open PR addresses the block-size-vs-`num_tokens` gap; #40413's test only compared `num_tokens=1` vs `4`, both below the 256 threshold, so it could not catch this.

## Test

**Both runs use this PR's updated test** (`test_fused_add_rms_norm_batch_invariant_residual_path`, the seed-swept version). The previous single-seed test (`seed=42`) passes on the buggy kernel, which is why it never caught this.
The decisive parameter is `n_extra`: `n_extra=299` makes `num_tokens=300 >= 256` (crossing the block-size threshold and exposing the bug), while `n_extra=3` (`num_tokens=4`) stays below it. That is why every failure below is an
`n_extra=299` case, and the seed is swept so a single lucky seed can't hide it.

subject: [AMD] Fix Aiter RMSNorm layout handling (#23974)
pr_body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes a ROCm/Aiter RMSNorm crash seen on MI325/gfx942 when Qwen3-style Q/K normalization passes strided higher-rank views into Aiter's RMSNorm path.

The SGLang-side fix keeps the Aiter backend enabled, but normalizes the input layout before calling Aiter:

- Already-safe 2D contiguous inputs stay on the zero-copy fast path.
- Strided or higher-rank inputs are made contiguous and flattened to 2D.
- The output is reshaped back to the original higher-rank shape.

## Root Cause

Qwen3 splits a packed QKV projection into Q/K/V views. Q and K can be shaped like:

```text
q: shape=(2048, 32, 128), stride=(6144, 128, 1)
k: shape=(2048,  8, 128), stride=(6144, 128, 1)
```

These are valid PyTorch views, but Aiter's RMSNorm kernels expect 2D contiguous input. Passing the strided 3D views directly to Aiter can memory-fault on MI325/gfx942.

## Fix

In `RMSNorm.forward_aiter()`:

```python
needs_reshape = x.dim() != 2 and residual is None
if needs_reshape:
    original_shape = x.shape
    x = x.contiguous().reshape(-1, original_shape[-1])
elif not x.is_contiguous():
    x = x.contiguous()

...

if needs_reshape:
    output = output.reshape(original_shape)
```

This is layout-gated, not architecture-gated. It avoids overhead for the normal 2D contiguous path and only copies when the input layout is unsafe for Aiter.

## Validation

### Direct Reproducer

Before the fix, directly calling the Aiter RMSNorm path on strided Q/K views reproduced:

```text
Memory access fault by GPU node-2
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

After the fix, the same strided Q/K RMSNorm probe succeeds:

```text
sglang aiter RMSNorm strided ok torch.Size([2048, 32, 128]) torch.Size([2048, 8, 128])
```

### Qwen3-8B Server

Launched Qwen3-8B on MI325/gfx942 with:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000 \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --disable-radix-cache \
    --cuda-graph-max-bs 2048 \
    --max-mamba-cache-size 15000 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.88
```

The server completed CUDA graph capture and served requests without the memory fault.

coder_B.counterfactual_rationale: The Aiter RMSNorm kernel faulted on strided higher-rank Q/K views that are valid PyTorch tensors but unsafe for the backend. Layout edge tests using non-contiguous 3D views on ROCm would plausibly reveal it.

subject: [Bugfix] Guard mixed-dtype allreduce RMSNorm quant fusions (#48330)

Fixes #48324.

The residual FlashInfer allreduce + RMSNorm + static-quantization patterns could
match graphs where the activation and RMSNorm weight have different dtypes.

This occurs with Qwen/Gemma-style RMSNorm in

RMSNorm weight is FP32 due to the `weight.float() + 1.0` computation. Selecting

produces repeated tokens such as `!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!`.

- `AllReduceFusedAddRMSNormStaticQuantFP8Pattern`
